name: Phragmites Adaptive Management Framework Small Grants (AAMP)
summary: Small grants to manage invasive non-native Phragmites in the US Great Lakes basin using priority management combinations, with grantees reporting monitoring and management data back to the adaptive management framework.

geography.label: U.S. Great Lakes basin and surrounding watersheds

amount.note: No funding cap; amounts outside the expected range are considered

reporting: Monitoring and seasonal management reports for each enrolled management unit, a semiannual financial report, and final reports and grant deliverables.

status.quote: APPLICATIONS FOR AAMP FUNDING IS CURRENTLY OPEN UNTIL APRIL 15TH, 2026!

opens.quote: Proposal Period: Accepting application proposals March 11 - April 15, 2026

deadline.quote: APPLICATIONS FOR AAMP FUNDING IS CURRENTLY OPEN UNTIL APRIL 15TH, 2026!

pool.quote: A projected total budget of $105,000 will be available to applicants

applicant_types.quote: Eligible Applicants: U.S.-based state, Tribal, or local units of government, lake associations/watershed protection groups, non-profit 501(c)(3) organizations, universities/colleges, conservation groups

geography.quote: Geographic Scope: U.S. Great Lakes basin and surrounding watersheds

access.quote: You may view the 2026 request for proposals (RFP) and template for proposals below

amount.quote: individual grants are generally expected to range from $5,000 to $30,000; there is no funding cap and amounts outside of the expected range will be considered

reporting.quote: Growing management report due for EACH enrolled MU. Note that management activities must conclude at least one month before monitoring in July. July 31, 2026 - Monitoring report 2 due for EACH enrolled MU; conclusion of grant activities. August 30, 2026 - Last submission of final reports and grant deliverables.
